name: Afterborn
tagline: Humans raised in the city’s shelters.
description: Humans with few or no body modifications. Their communities share medicine, meals, and shelter.
lore: The first Afterborn were children left out of the evacuation census. Shelter cooks wrote their names on meal bowls so they would still receive rations. Their descendants keep that practice. Your character’s quests trace missing clinic records, remove ancestry checks, and follow the water supply back to Mourning Fen. Oru asks you to carry the names behind those bowls into the Living Record, including everyone still waiting for care.

name: Lattice
description: Their memories are stored in ceramic bodies. A memory can be copied, but each person can choose their own life.

passive.name: Extra energy
passive.description: Start with 20 extra maximum energy for abilities.

lore: During the Long Brownout, repair machines used damaged human records to recognize their patients. Some developed memories and wishes of their own. Tam of Nine Cups became the first recognized Lattice citizen. Your character’s quests challenge seizure for unpaid debts and forced merging, then investigate the mineral seam used to make replacement bodies. Your account in the Living Record keeps each chosen name beside the material cost of keeping that person alive.

name: Revenant
tagline: People brought back to life after death.
description: Revenants live in new bodies and may remember their earlier lives. They choose whether they want to be brought back again.

passive.name: More critical hits
passive.description: Add 3 percentage points to your chance of a critical hit, which deals extra damage.

lore: The first restoration vaults served workers repairing Vesper’s sea barriers. Contractors later used restoration agreements to claim those workers’ labor. Your character’s quests uncover the hidden terms, free people from collection orders, and set new consent rules while the clinics face a shortage of water and nutrients. Your account in the Living Record asks what a second life owes—and what no creditor may claim from it.

name: Sporebound
tagline: People whose bodies live with helpful fungi.
description: Their fungal partners help them filter poisons and move faster. Each partnership needs its own food and care.
lore: Companies developed these cultures to protect salt miners, then charged the miners to keep them alive. Workers shared recipes that ended their dependence on the licensed feed. Your character’s quests investigate that history, protect patients from seizure, and contain escaped strains that are spreading through the salt pans. Your account in the Living Record keeps the hosts, caretakers, and displaced households visible beside the culture’s survival.
